newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone, Nigerian troops try to ease tension.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone, Nigerian troops try to ease tension.

text.p: FREETOWN, June 11, Reuter - Sierra Leone and Nigerian senior military officers met in Freetown on Wednesday to try to reduce tension following fighting near the international airport during the night.
The two sides agreed to talk to their men in an effort to cool the situation, a Sierra Leone military spokesman said.
Nigerian troops holding the island airport of Lungi off the capital killed seven rebels allied with the Sierra Leone army in the clash on Tuesday night, the spokesman said.
The shooting caused panic in Freetown where many fear a Nigerian attack to restore president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah who was ousted in a coup on May 25.
The coup makers are backed by rebels of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF), who were involved in the fighting near the airport with units of the Nigerian-led West African ECOMOG force.
After the meeting Sierra Leone officers went to army barracks near the airport and spoke to troops there, appealing to them to observe restraint and avoid confrontation with the ECOMOG force.
Sierra Leone military sources said the Nigerians had promised to release a number of prisoners taken during Tuesday night's fighting.
Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown last week in a show of force but failed to prevent the coup makers from naming their own ruling council.

A tense calm has prevailed, with the coup leaders saying they would consider fresh elections but would not have Kabbah back. They accuse him of stalling on peace with the rebels and humiliating the army and fomenting ethnic hatred by arming Kamajor traditional hunter militias.
The RUF rebels took up arms against the Sierra Leone army in 1991 but have flooded into Freetown since the coup to take the side of their former foes.
